clue.text: Passport rejected, man being female!

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word for the document is turned round

parts.note: a passport is a form of ID, identification
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: An outraged official refuses someone's travel document on discovering the bearer is a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' looks like a noun opposed to 'female', but it is a verb: to man a desk is to staff it.
explanation.definitionFit: The distaff side of a family is the female line, from the spinning staff traditionally used by women.

clue.text: Controversial topic: bad mail and good mail unchecked in here

indicators.note: controversial means contested or disputed, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A disputed issue: post of every kind passing through without inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Controversial' scrambles TOPIC BAD MAIL; 'mail' appears twice, once as fodder and once in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Embassy pouches are immune from customs inspection, so their correspondence passes unexamined.

clue.text: Pipe about average, mean

indicators.note: about means the verb goes round the norm

parts.note: to pipe is to sing in a high voice
par is the average or normal standard

explanation.surface: Someone smoking a middling pipe, being stingy about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mean with money means being frugal or stingy.

clue.text: An agreeable, less conservative, musical

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: less means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: nice means agreeable

explanation.surface: A pleasant musical show that is less politically conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: The Broadway show about the orphan with the song 'Tomorrow' is a musical.

clue.text: Food served with a burger in a kind of beef

definitions.note: plural sense: beef can mean cattle bred for meat, here one such animal

parts.note: chips, called fries in American usage, come with a burger

indicators.note: kind of means a sort or version of, so the two short words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A menu item: chips alongside a burger made from some breed of cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind of' looks like part of the definition but jumbles IN A into IAN; 'beef' here means a beast reared for meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Friesians are a black-and-white cattle breed, also raised as beef animals.

clue.text: Find retro Spanish article about Mexican food

indicators.note: retro means harking backwards, so the whole assembly is read in reverse
about means surrounding, so the article goes round the food

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine definite article, 'the'
a taco is a filled Mexican tortilla

explanation.surface: A puzzle about tracking down an old-fashioned Spanish word linked to tortillas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' applies to the whole assembly, not just the article.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something and to pinpoint its whereabouts are synonyms.

clue.text: Red trombone's ending with pink organ in story

indicators.note: in means the inner letters go inside the word for the fib

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib

indicators.note: ending means the last letter of the word

parts.note: the Financial Times, printed on pink paper, is a newspaper or organ

explanation.surface: A tale of an organ and a trombone, red and pink, sounds like a band's colourful story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' here means a newspaper; this puzzle's own paper is pink.
explanation.definitionFit: A Red is a left-winger, a socialist or communist in political slang.

clue.text: Check prisoner's discipline

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner, plus the possessive S
to train is to discipline

explanation.surface: A prison inspection of an inmate's behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to restrain or restrict it.

clue.text: Port more flavoursome

definitions.meaning: a Moroccan city on the Strait of Gibraltar
having a sharper, zestier taste, comparative of a tart-tasting adjective

explanation.surface: Port wine with an extra kick.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a Moroccan seaport; the comparative of 'tangy' means sharper in taste.

clue.text: Somone in court spat on no oil painting

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the word for the quarrel follows the word for the looks

parts.note: 'no oil painting' is a British idiom for an unattractive person, i.e. plain
a spat is a petty quarrel, a tiff

explanation.surface: Someone in court spits on an unremarkable canvas, a scene of courtroom vandalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somone' is the clue's own misprint for 'Someone'. 'no oil painting' is British slang for someone not good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: The party who brings a lawsuit is a person appearing in court.

clue.text: Figure in book group

indicators.note: in means the number sits inside the abbreviation for the scriptures

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible
one is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A number appearing in a book club or similar group.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical ensemble of nine players is a type of group.

clue.text: Slow, as is "sentimental"?

definitions.meaning: taking up lots of hours, protracted
the word sentimental swallows the word for hours and minutes in its middle

explanation.surface: A slow, mushy film or song, described in one word.
explanation.walkthrough: S-EN-TIME-NTAL: the second reading treats 'consuming' literally, as swallowing up.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow task eats up hours; and the clue word literally holds a span of hours inside it.

clue.text: Wire alongside circuit, a shade of green

indicators.note: alongside means the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a circuit is a ring, shaped like the letter O
the live wire carries current in a plug

explanation.surface: Electrical instructions: a wire running beside a circuit, with a colour code thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour of the unripe fruit gives its name to a dull yellowish-green hue.

clue.text: Bone is buried in male religion

parts.note: the shinbone, the tibia

indicators.note: buried in means placed inside, so the word goes within the male animal

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bone buried with a man, suggesting an ancient faith's burial rite.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional Japanese faith centred on kami spirits is a religion.

clue.text: Doctor in a large African native

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician working at large in some place, or a doctor in a big way.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born in Algeria is a native of a North African country.

clue.text: People follow a course

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
to track someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A crowd heading off along a set route.
explanation.definitionFit: A circuit for horses or cars is a course.

clue.text: Great wrench to cut material

parts.note: fab, short for fabulous, means great

indicators.note: the word for the sprain is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a rick is a wrench or sprain of a joint

explanation.surface: A handy wrench being just the tool for cutting cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' docks RICK of its K.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth or textile is called material.

clue.text: Love child who has translated Norse!

indicators.note: has means the first word is joined by what follows

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: translated means rendered into another form, so the letters of the language name are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An illegitimate child who has rendered old Scandinavian texts into English.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for a bastard, a child born outside marriage.

clue.text: Bug home and dry with first bit of tapping

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
sec is French for dry, used of wine

indicators.note: the first bit of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A phone-tap bug planted at home, with a dry first test of the tapping.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's bug is a listening device; the definition wants a creepy-crawly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bug is a common informal word for a small creature like a beetle.

clue.text: Drink in outskirts of Srinagar, certainly not an Italian port

indicators.note: in means the drink goes inside the outer letters
outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
certainly not is an emphatic no

explanation.surface: Drinking on the fringes of an Indian city, firmly denied to be an Italian harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Salerno is a seaport on the Gulf of Salerno in southern Italy.

clue.text: Hit after hit bringing cheers

indicators.note: after means one word follows the other

parts.note: to chin someone is to hit them on the chin
again, to chin is to punch on the jaw

explanation.surface: One blow after another in a fight, then a celebratory toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Chin-chin is an old-fashioned drinking toast, like saying cheers.

clue.text: Crazy, crazy way to divide rent

indicators.note: to divide means to split the other word, sitting in its middle

parts.note: to rent is to hire

indicators.note: crazy means wild, so the letters of the word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mad way to split the rent between flatmates.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'crazy's do different jobs: the first is the definition, the second jumbles the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone haywire is out of control, wildly erratic.

clue.text: Jerk missing part of morgage, bad speller

parts.note: the clue's misspelt 'morgage' lacks one letter of mortgage; that missing part is the letter needed
a witch casts spells, a speller with bad intent

explanation.surface: A jerk who cannot spell 'mortgage' properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The misspelling is deliberate: 'morgage' is short of the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerk is a sudden spasmodic movement.

clue.text: One crying about tinnitus, initially, where ringing takes place

indicators.note: about means the shouter surrounds the letter

parts.note: a bellower is someone who cries out loudly

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tinnitus sufferer crying out about the ringing in their ears.
explanation.walkthrough: Ringing seems to be tinnitus; it is church bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower housing bells is where change ringing happens.

clue.text: Bashful and Happy rolled over rodent

parts.note: coy means bashful or shy

indicators.note: rolled over means turned upside down, so the short word is reversed

parts.note: to feel up is to be happy

explanation.surface: Two of Snow White's dwarfs, Bashful and Happy, tumbling over a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American aquatic rodent, also called nutria.

clue.text: Fine form

definitions.meaning: classy, of high quality and elegance

explanation.definitionFit: Class means excellence or style; a class is also a form or year group in school.

clue.text: Irish force a draw after a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: to draw a cart is to drag it

explanation.surface: An Irish team draws a match after fighting back from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garda Síochána is the police service of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Opera season's ending in ignominy, primarily, for maestro

parts.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera

indicators.note: ending means the last letter of the word
primarily means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An opera season ends in disgrace, with the conductor to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian conductor, a maestro of the podium.

clue.text: Articulated forward pipe

indicators.note: articulated means spoken, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: in rugby the hooker is a forward in the front row of the scrum

explanation.surface: An articulated pipe that bends forward, like a flexible tube.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the rugby position sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A water pipe for smoking tobacco through water is called this.

clue.text: Savings in bag get sent back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Money squirrelled away in a bag that then gets posted back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into the words, and 'back' reads GGETSEN in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve of money set aside for the future is a common idiom for savings.
